Please explain the difference between strategy and tactics

In simplest terms strategy is the over all plan to accomplish something. It could be to win a war, win a game, or some other objective you have. Tactics are those individual things you employ to achieve your objective. I will start with some that most people understand. Football is a combination of strategy and tactic. Coaches lay out a strategy to win a game. It is a list events they desire to see happen. Lets say the opposing team has a super passing defense. Well a coach playing against then would likely go with a rushing attack to take advantage of their weak rushing defense.

In a war or strategy based game like chess or checkers or even backgammon It is the big picture of how the game or war will end with you winning. For Instance WWII the allied strategy was to weaken the axis power to the point that an invasion would be successful.

Tactics on the other hand are the smaller things done to achieve the ultimate goal. Back to the football scenario. Your apposing team has a strong passing defense but it has a fatal flaw say that team has staked all of its dependence on that passing defense. It has a sort of arrogance that no one can beat them because their passing defense is so strong. They put no effort at all into a running defense. So as a tactic you might start out drawing them out with an early passing game. Build up a false sense of security with a passing game to start. That is a tactic. The next tactic would be to then switch to a running game and score some quick points. This demoralizes them. Then you might throw in some trick plays where you get them to believe you will pass and instead run the ball. They lose their edge. To further make it difficult you set up for a running play and draw them into that and instead pass and they are not ready and you have some successful plays. Those smaller goals and how they are accomplished are tactics.

Back to WWII the tactics were things like forcing the axis to fight on two fronts, thus weakening their over all defenses. Also night and day bombing of their war making machine destroyed much of their ability to stay in the battle. They were already extended when they cross the Mediterranean into north Africa. So the first thing was to defeat that over extension which happened early in the war. Then from their the two pronged invasion of Europe was put into motion. The defeat in Africa was part strategic and part tactical It was strategic in it was part of the over all plan and tactical in that it was done first. The strategic plan of invading Europe was then achieved with the tactic of a two pronged assault, a southern one and a norther one. Those were large scale tactics. In the norther invasion one tactic was to create a false idea of where the invasion would take place. Fake troop build ups were set up and left to be easily seen by the axis powers as to draw their forces to protect an area that was not going to be invaded and then the switch came and they invaded the area that the axis powers though they had enough protection of because of the difficulty of an assault there. Once they had landed they quickly surrounded the built up defenses and cut them off from supply lines and then advanced onto the final objective.

In say chess you strategy to win is to control the center of the board. Your tactics could be to occupy that area directly or another option is to over see that area such that moves into it will create costly losses. By utilizing the differing allowed moves of pieces you can put pieces in the center which can attack outward. Or if you want control with over sight you can set up on the perimeter and attack as your opponent is forced to the center of the board.

So to boil it all down strategy is the plan to achieve your goal and tactics are the means and methods employed to get there. Two great books that deal with both deal with real war but also can be used in other areas. First is the Chinese book by Sun Tzu, The Art of War. A second is Go Rin no Sho or the Book of Five Rings by Misashi Miyamoto. They are books on both strategy and tactics and often referred to by military types develop their strategies as well as tactics. The combine both the plan(strategy) and the moves(tactics) and stitch them together to create and overall strategy. In so doing they employ various tactics as well as philosophical understandings of battle and human nature to achieve an ultimate victory.

Hope that helps.
